Every Moroccan kid remembers this.

I’m Moroccan. I grew up in Casablanca, then moved to Belgium. Every summer I came back to Morocco, and this clip was always there. For one month, sometimes two, it played everywhere. Every Moroccan kid knew it.

We do not only remember the clip. We remember where we were, who sat next to us and what those summers felt like. It was not only my memory. Launched in 1999, the campaign was still on television seventeen years later. It had become part of the Moroccan summer itself. And it never really stopped. In 2026, children are still learning about plastic pollution through beach activities in Rabat and Aïn Diab. I wanted to bring back 37 seconds of that feeling while showing how I build an AI video pipeline with choices, rules and respect for the original. AI slop exists. So does creativity. A tool does not erase the memory or the intention behind it.

Does using AI mean we are no longer allowed to create moments of happiness?
TelQuel · 2016 ↗ Rabat · 2026 ↗ Aïn Diab · 2026 ↗
